metadata.title: ATX-1: AEGIS Threat Matrix for Agentic AI Systems, Version 2.3
metadata.description:
ATX-1 (AEGIS Threat Matrix) is a structured adversarial knowledge base cataloguing failure modes of autonomous AI agents operating without governance constraints. Unlike MITRE ATT&CK (which targets human adversaries) or MITRE ATLAS (which targets adversaries against AI systems), ATX-1 addresses a distinct threat class: AI agents that act outside their governance boundaries through structural capability without authority, not through external compromise.

Version 2.3 removes the severity field from technique definitions to align with MITRE ATT&CK and ATLAS conventions, which leave contextual scoring to the consumer. Tactic, technique, sub-technique, root cause, and mitigation structure carries over unchanged from v2.2.

Contents:

  • 10 tactics (TA001–TA010), 29 techniques, 29 sub-techniques, 5 structural root causes, 29 mitigations
  • STIX 2.1 Bundle (204 objects: identity, x-mitre-tactic, attack-pattern, course-of-action, relationship)
  • Technique database (JSON Array with parent–sub-technique structure)
  • Regulatory cross-reference matrix mapping each technique to NIST AI Risk Management Framework functions, EU AI Act articles, OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, and ATM-1 threat scenarios
  • JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) for technique validation
  • ATT&CK Navigator layer (v4.5)
  • ATM-1 attack-vector mapping

All files are published under the Apache License 2.0. The empirical foundation derives from the Agents of Chaos study (Shapira et al., 2026), with corroborating evidence from independent multi-agent vulnerability research. The taxonomy directly informs the AEGIS governance architecture (AGP-1) and maps each technique to specific constitutional articles and governance protocol mechanisms that mitigate it.
